repository_role: FCP development lane only; not part of the active New Phytologist manuscript and not a modification of CHUN Evolution Letters v0.3.
programme_question: Do the same biological properties predict how rapidly biological information is lost across evolutionary time and geographic space, for both organismal traits and biotic interaction identities?
focal_unit: one biologically coherent radiation/system; temporal and spatial summaries are aggregated to the system level before cross-system inference

trait_time.question: How rapidly does trait similarity above a system-specific null decay with relative phylogenetic divergence?
trait_time.similarity: Gower similarity for mixed traits or 1 - standardized Euclidean distance for continuous-only traits, fixed before outcomes within each trait family
trait_time.distance: relative patristic distance scaled within radiation to [0,1]
trait_time.sign: larger lambda = faster evolutionary memory loss
trait_time.minimum_design: at least 20 focal taxa with one frozen phylogeny and a common trait representation

trait_space.question: How rapidly does trait similarity decline across geographic separation within the same radiation?
trait_space.similarity: same trait representation as trait_time; repeated population/individual measurements only
trait_space.distance: great-circle distance or a frozen landscape distance; one primary distance chosen before trait outcomes
trait_space.minimum_design: at least 5 focal species with at least 20 georeferenced trait observations each, or an equivalently prequalified repeated-population design

interaction_time.question: How rapidly does partner-profile similarity decline with focal-species phylogenetic divergence?
interaction_time.similarity: 1 - Jensen-Shannon divergence between normalized partner profiles after a frozen partner-opportunity rule
interaction_time.opportunity_control: phylogenetic pair is evaluable only under a frozen shared-partner-opportunity frame or a null preserving partner availability
interaction_time.sign: larger lambda = faster evolutionary loss of interaction identity
interaction_time.minimum_design: at least 20 focal taxa with interaction profiles and an evaluable partner-opportunity model

interaction_space.question: How rapidly do realized interaction identities turn over across geography?
interaction_space.total_turnover: interaction beta diversity across spatial networks
interaction_space.sign: larger lambda = faster geographic interaction turnover/rewiring
interaction_space.minimum_design: at least 5 spatially distinct networks or population interaction samples with comparable effort semantics

context_heterogeneity.definition: pre-outcome composite of abiotic heterogeneity and partner-opportunity heterogeneity; both components must be available, standardized within system, and averaged with equal weight; no one-component renormalization
context_heterogeneity.interpretation: systems exposed to more heterogeneous abiotic and biotic contexts should lose state identity faster in both time and space

specialization.definition: effective specialization = 1 - normalized partner/niche entropy, computed from an outcome-independent or separately frozen resource/partner frame
specialization.interpretation: specialists should conserve partner identity and show less rewiring among co-occurring partners, while being more exposed to partner replacement

dispersal_mobility.definition: independently measured movement or dispersal-capacity axis, standardized within major taxonomic group; no proxy chosen after response inspection
dispersal_mobility.interpretation: greater movement should homogenize geography without necessarily erasing phylogenetic memory

fixed_strata.rule: interaction type is a predeclared stratum/moderator, not a fourth free predictor
fixed_strata.rationale: prior work already shows phylogenetic signal can differ between antagonistic and mutualistic networks; the programme tests whether time-space coupling differs as well

requirements: all four response estimands physically recoverable
all three predictor axes frozen before response fitting
taxon identity crosswalk exact or predeclared
temporal and spatial data refer to the same focal radiation
interaction spatial turnover can be decomposed into species turnover and rewiring
both temporal and spatial responses available within either trait domain or interaction domain
all predictors required for the declared hypothesis available before response fitting
cannot be promoted as full four-response evidence

programme_gate.failure_action: HOLD; do not lower system counts or broaden response definitions after seeing outcomes

primary_tests.T1_shared_context_acceleration: Across systems, P1 context heterogeneity has a positive effect on both time and space loss rates in both response domains.
primary_tests.T2_time_space_coupling: Within each response domain, system-level temporal loss rate positively covaries with spatial turnover after the three predictors are frozen.
primary_tests.T3_specialization_decoupling: P2 specialization predicts slower interaction-memory loss and lower rewiring, but a larger species-turnover component under partner replacement.
primary_tests.T4_mobility_decoupling: P3 mobility predicts weaker spatial turnover with no required temporal-memory effect.
primary_tests.T5_interaction_type_modification: The T2/T3 interaction-domain relationships may differ between mutualistic and antagonistic strata; direction is not chosen post hoc.

nulls_and_controls.trait_null: preserve trait marginal distribution and declared phylogenetic/spatial opportunity while breaking trait-to-distance assignment
nulls_and_controls.interaction_time_null: preserve focal degree/partner availability under the frozen opportunity model
nulls_and_controls.interaction_space_null: preserve local species pools and link totals; rewiring tested only among co-occurring species
nulls_and_controls.source_identity: study/network/database identity is clustered; multiple networks from one programme are not independent systems

hard_nonclaims: flower colour is not the target trait class
phylogenetic signal in ecological networks is not claimed as novel
spatial interaction turnover is not equated with rewiring
species turnover is not interpreted as partner switching
one universal turnover constant is not assumed
trait and interaction responses are not pooled at the row level
a system failing any opportunity or effort gate is not treated as a zero effect

relation_to_existing_programmes.CHUN: proof-of-concept temporal memory axis for one phenotype family
relation_to_existing_programmes.FCP: proof-of-concept geographic organization axis and reusable disttrait machinery
relation_to_existing_programmes.IWE: interaction-phenology evidence source, not automatically an eligible turnover system
